topics.flagship-ru-ua: Russia said Ukraine launched more than 2,000 drones in a single day, the largest attack of the war by its account, and the Crimea bridge was reportedly hit. Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts (5 outlets). Estonia says it will close Russia border crossings after an attempted arson attack on a drone factory, which it blames on Russia and the Kremlin denies. Atomic safety regulators warn the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is rising this winter because of attacks on power infrastructure, and Ukraine is preparing for Ramstein Group and Coalition of the Willing meetings this week.
topics.flagship-ir-il: An Israeli air strike killed a senior Hamas military commander in Khan Younis (3 outlets). Separately, the USS Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East, joining two other carriers in CENTCOM, amid speculation about whether the US-Iran war will resume. Single-source reports say Iran launched new drones at Bahrain while Trump signals a waiting game. Houthi forces have reportedly advanced to within 100 km of Aden, putting Saudi crude exports at risk, and the UK and allies are pressing Israel to allow rapid aid into Gaza, where children are reported dying from hypothermia.
topics.T15: The most detailed item is a Red Cross appeal on exceptional flooding in northeast Argentina. It reports 4,190 displaced, 2 dead, and a Paraná River still above evacuation levels, with a second flood wave forecast and an El Niño expected to keep waters high into early 2027. No national or provincial emergency has been declared. The other items are minor and unrelated: Pemberton Valley evacuation alerts lifted, a cargo ship sinking in the Black Sea with all 12 crew rescued, California wave damage, and UK resilience and preparedness reports.
topics.T01: A Sudanese army airstrike killed at least 13 people in West Kordofan, according to a local rights group (4 outlets). Five international organizations separately called for a halt to Sudan hostilities and condemned drone attacks on civilians and power stations. The Saudi-led coalition reportedly intercepted two missiles and two drones over Riyadh as fighting escalated in Yemen's Marib and al-Jawf. Trump is heading to Asia for a reported trilateral summit with Putin and Xi (4 outlets).
topics.T02: Coverage is sparse and mixed. A nine-month-old baby reportedly died of hypothermia in a Gaza displacement tent as winter returns. The UN welcomed Libya's amendments raising the minimum military recruitment age to 18. Other items are commentary on genocide definitions ahead of an ICJ ruling on Myanmar, and a Nigerian candidate's pledge on women and children.
topics.T03: Eight outlets carry reports that Iran has alleged plans to target Trump officials, and the coverage frames this as a possible 'dirty bomb' threat. The reported planning includes specific locations and targets, which has raised security concerns. The input gives no further detail and the claims are unverified.
topics.T04: Coverage is mostly generic or dated. One report says Ebola has killed more than 5,000 people in the DRC, and that health workers at a treatment center in Ituri walked off the job after four months without pay. A Sudan dengue study documents 13,371 cases across ten states. The remaining items are COVID commentary, a quarantine lawsuit settlement, and a research paper, with no clear new outbreak signal.
topics.T05: UN Secretary-General Guterres backed ASEAN's fresh diplomatic efforts to engage Myanmar's post-coup government while stressing the need for a return to 'true democracy'. NATO is scaling back high-level meetings and will not hold a leaders' summit in Albania next year, amid tension over defense spending, Iran and Ukraine (2 outlets). Israeli opposition leader Lapid accused Netanyahu's Likud of attempting a 'coup' (no outlets counted). The other items are analysis pieces on Sudan and Venezuela.
topics.T06: More than 100 people have been arrested after riots in Dublin that followed Riad Bouchaker's attempted murder of three children on Parnell Street, with more cases before the courts (4 outlets). Other items are single-source and mostly unrelated: Delhi riots charges, an arrest in Bangladesh's July Uprising murder case, garment worker wage protests, and youth-led protests and strikes in Germany and France.
topics.T08: Security forces in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir, killed one militant and reportedly had another trapped after an attack on a CRPF post last week that injured three personnel (7 outlets). A coronial inquest heard that a 16-year-old shot dead by police in an Australian terror incident was probably self-radicalised and acted alone. Other single-source items include the arrest of a Spanish neo-Nazi figure with a large weapons cache, a Nigerian military ambush in Katsina, and a report on persecution of Christians.
topics.T10: Congressional defense budget politics dominate. The $1.45 trillion FY2027 request appears dead after the midterms, and Senate Republicans are reportedly shifting about $69B from reconciliation into a roughly $1.1 trillion appropriations bill. The bill funds munitions, air and missile defense, drones and shipbuilding, with $750 million for Ukraine. A UN conference is considering rules on lethal AI weapons (2 outlets), and India and Japan are pursuing artillery, naval and production-surge plans.
topics.T11: An India-Myanmar naval exercise concluded off Visakhapatnam (5 outlets). India and Sri Lanka began Exercise Mitra Shakti XII, running November 13-26. Kuwait and France held a first planning meeting for the 2027 Pearl of the West exercise, and Australian troops are testing jungle armour in a joint exercise.
topics.T12: A Microsoft 365 outage led to 15 hotel guests in Germany suffering chlorine gas poisoning (4 outlets), and users reported fresh Microsoft problems on Monday. Google reportedly says Russian speakers carried out the first fully automated AI cyberattack, and the FBI warned about an AI-powered attacker toolkit it calls ARTEX. German drone maker Quantum Systems reportedly suffered a cyberattack and the German military grounded its drones. Osaka city also reportedly suffered a cyberattack exposing over a million email addresses, and a US air traffic control communications failure was also reported.
topics.T13: Coverage is thin. The British government is accused of refusing to release full migrant crime statistics, and one unverified report (no outlets counted) says 3,684 unauthorized migrants arrived on El Hierro in the Canary Islands within days.
topics.T14: The US Embassy in Madrid issued a security advisory warning of possible terrorist attacks at holiday markets and transport hubs across Europe (3 outlets). Iran's embassy in South Africa reportedly posted photos and names of two US Navy officers who commanded USS Spruance, with an explicit threat against them.
topics.T16: Martine Moise, widow of Haiti's slain president, is among 33 registered candidates in Haiti's first presidential election in a decade (4 outlets). In Israel, Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot demands a probe of the Prime Minister's Office over allegations it fabricated election fraud claims (4 outlets), while Likud denies this and seeks more time to appeal the results. Other items cover Lula's reported reelection in Brazil, Sweden's stalled prime ministerial talks 64 days after its election, French presidential contenders, and Atiku's 2027 campaign pledge.

bluf: Russia reported the biggest Ukrainian drone attack of the war, with more than 2,000 drones launched in one day, and the Crimea bridge was reportedly hit while Kyiv endured a record 17 air raid alerts. A Sudanese army airstrike killed at least 13 people in West Kordofan, according to a local rights group, as the army-paramilitary war enters its fourth year. Haiti's first presidential election in a decade has 33 registered candidates, including Martine Moise, widow of the slain president. In Kashmir, one militant involved in last week's attack on a CRPF post was killed in a Kulgam encounter, and a second was reportedly trapped. In Dublin, more than 100 people have been arrested over riots following Riad Bouchaker's attempted murder of three children, with more cases before the courts. Estonia says it will close Russia border crossings after an attempted arson attack on a drone factory, which it blames on Russia and the Kremlin denies. Houthi forces have also reportedly advanced to within 100 km of Aden, putting Saudi crude exports at risk.
